name: Residence card for family members of EU/EEA citizens (FreizügG/EU)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires being the spouse, registered partner, child under 21, or a dependent relative of an EU/EEA citizen (other than a German citizen) who is exercising free movement rights in Germany.

This requires the EU/EEA sponsor to be genuinely exercising free-movement rights in Germany (e.g. working, studying, or self-sufficient) — this route does NOT generally apply to family members of German citizens, who instead need a residence permit under § 28 AufenthG unless the German exercised free movement in another member state first.

evidence_required.document: Proof of the family relationship (marriage/partnership/birth certificate)
Proof of the EU/EEA sponsor's exercise of free movement in Germany

notes: Structurally distinct from de_family_reunification_spouse: this route derives from EU free-movement law (FreizügG/EU), not the Aufenthaltsgesetz, and the residence card CERTIFIES a right that already exists rather than creating one — it carries unrestricted work rights immediately and no income/housing/language pre-conditions, a materially easier route than the standard Ehegattennachzug when it applies. Key eligibility trap flagged explicitly per the research: this does NOT generally cover family members of GERMAN citizens — those need § 28 AufenthG instead, UNLESS the German sponsor previously exercised free movement in another EU member state (the 'Surinder Singh' scenario), which is a genuinely obscure but consequential distinction most applicants would never find on their own — exactly the kind of blocker_text value-add this product is meant to provide. citizenship_after_months (120) reflects the standard 5-year settlement plus 5-year naturalisation stacking, since this route's holder doesn't get any of the accelerated timelines available to Blue Card or spouse-of-German paths — genuinely the slowest family route in the German dataset, worth surfacing in any cross-route comparison.
